description: Rules and conventions the task's gold depends on. Published so that no legitimate answer can be marked wrong on a convention the task never stated.
element_order_note: Hill order: carbon first, hydrogen second, then other elements alphabetically. Formulas must be rendered in this order so two correct answers cannot differ in string form.
naive_assembly_rule: Sum the molecular formulas of the monomers loaded by the annotated modules, in module order, then subtract one H2O for each peptide bond formed. A linear assembly of n monomers forms n-1 peptide bonds.
residual_rule: residual = product_formula - naive_assembly_formula, element by element, signed. Negative counts are retained.

verdict_rules.balanced: every residual element count is zero
verdict_rules.cyclisation_only: the residual is exactly H:-2, O:-1 (loss of one further water, consistent with macrocyclisation or lactonisation)
verdict_rules.additional_chemistry_required: any residual element count is positive, i.e. the product contains atoms the annotated modules do not supply
verdict_rules.deficit_unexplained: all non-zero residual counts are negative but the residual is not exactly H:-2, O:-1
verdict_rules.insufficient: the entry does not annotate a monomer for every module, so no assembly formula can be computed

verdict_precedence_note: Evaluated in this order; the first matching rule applies. Precedence is declared because 'additional_chemistry_required' and 'deficit_unexplained' could otherwise both be argued for a mixed-sign residual.
scope_note: MIBiG annotates the enzymatic module count, which is not the number of monomer incorporations in the final product: iterative module reuse, non-NRPS moieties such as fatty-acid starters and prenyl groups, and metal coordination all break the correspondence. Only 1 of 43 admissible entries is exactly balanced and 4 differ by one water, so a non-zero residual is the normal case and quantifying it is the task, not a defect to be explained away.
